summary_paragraph: An elderly female with a history of chronic microcytic anemia, recurrent venous thromboembolism on anticoagulation, and mild dementia was admitted due to a supratherapeutic INR of 8.7 and symptomatic anemia with hemoglobin of 6.0 g/dL. She presented with generalized weakness but denied any signs of active gastrointestinal bleeding. She received intravenous vitamin K to reverse the anticoagulant effect and one unit of packed red blood cells, with improvement in hemoglobin to 8.0 g/dL. No evidence of acute hemorrhage was found on clinical evaluation or rectal exam. Her warfarin dose was reduced from 2 mg to 1 mg daily, and enoxaparin was initiated for bridging therapy. She remained hemodynamically stable, with no complications during the admission. She was discharged home with follow-up arranged with primary care, the anticoagulation clinic, and hematology, along with instructions to resume all home medications and monitor for weight changes.
problems: Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
Anticoagulants causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
